wash.title: Does washing your hair more often damage it?
wash.text:
A 2021 study compared washing every day with once a week. Daily washing came out ahead on every measure, and no hair damage was found.

Two catches: Procter & Gamble paid for the study, and it didn't study curly or coily hair. For tightly coiled hair, the American Academy of Dermatology suggests washing every week or two.

Source: Punyani S, et al. The Impact of Shampoo Wash Frequency on Scalp and Hair Conditions. Skin Appendage Disord. 2021. PMID 34055906 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34055906)

float.title: The float test can't tell your hair porosity
float.text:
No study has shown the hair float test measures porosity. What lab work does show: porosity follows damage. In one study, bleach nearly tripled hair's surface area within the first minute.

So porosity isn't set by curl type: 4C hair can be low, normal or high porosity. Bleached or heat-damaged hair? Treat it as more porous.

Source: Hessefort Y, et al. True porosity measurement of hair. J Cosmet Sci. 2008. PMID 18818850 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18818850)

oil.title: Oil doesn't moisturize your hair. Water does.
oil.text:
In a lab study, an oil film reduced how much water hair took in, and also slowed water leaving. So apply your water-based product first and oil last, to seal it in.

And not every oil gets inside the hair: coconut oil did, mineral oil stayed on the surface. Jojoba, avocado and almond oil haven't been tested.

Sources:
Keis K, et al. Effect of oil films on moisture vapor absorption on human hair. J Cosmet Sci. 2007. PMID 17520153
Ruetsch SB, et al. Penetration of coconut and mineral oils into human hair fibers. J Cosmet Sci. 2001. PMID 11413497
